This is the fallback path for `_nullpager` and the no-command branches, where the stream is the real `sys.stdout`. When that new wrapper is garbage-collected, `IOBase` finalization calls `close()` on the shared underlying buffer, which closes the process's real stdout buffer. The fix is to avoid re-wrapping a buffer that another object still owns, for example by writing through the original stream and stripping ANSI in the write path without creating a second owner.

comments.body: Regression in masking coverage. The old code fell back to a generic message whenever the raw value appeared anywhere in the error (plain substring match). `_mask_hidden_input` only masks the raw value when it is delimited by non-word characters, so a secret that appears as a prefix or substring of a longer word is shown verbatim. Example: with hide_input=True and a custom type that fails with f"invalid input {value}s", entering "secret" yields "invalid input secrets", which exposes the full secret. The same applies to any value embedded in a longer token (e.g. "hunter2abc"). For a password-masking feature this is a leak that the previous code did not have. The PR's own test comment says the word-boundary rule is meant to avoid false positives, but for hidden input the safe default is to over-mask, not under-mask.

The docstring says the empty string is skipped, but the code does not skip it. With value == "", the pattern `(?<!\w)(?!\w)` matches at every position between non-word characters, so `'***'` is inserted into unrelated text such as ': ' boundaries and string ends. Either add an explicit `if value:` guard, which also fixes the docstring contract, or correct the docstring. The `if value is not None` check is also dead code because `value` is typed as `str`.

The new code is `self.file_okay and rv == dash`, so with `allow_dash=False` a literal `-` is still treated as the dash sentinel. comments.body: `__copy__` now mutates the source model. `self.__dict__['root'] = copy(self.__dict__['root'])` replaces the original instance's root with a new object, and this is a side effect of a shallow copy. Because `new_dict` is copied before this line, `new_dict['root']` is the old root object, which is now detached from `self`. Two problems follow. First, any reference the caller already holds to `original.root` is no longer the object the original model uses. Second, the copy shares the old root object with that caller reference, not with `self`. Example: `r = m.root; c = m.model_copy(); r.append(4)` changes `c.root` but not `m.root`, which inverts the expected relationship. The copy should be `new_dict['root'] = copy(self.__dict__['root'])` with `self.__dict__` left untouched. The new test only checks the copy's own root against the original's current root, so it does not catch this. The suite also cannot run at this head (pydantic-core version mismatch), so no probe here establishes correctness.

comments.body: The guard `if not try_eval_type is not None:` parses as `not (try_eval_type is not None)`. When `try_eval_type` is missing (`getattr` returned None, as on Pydantic versions that lack it), the condition is True and the code calls `None(value, globalns, localns)`, which raises TypeError. When it is present, the condition is False and the code falls through to the deprecated `eval_type_lenient` path, so the new branch is never used. Every string annotation resolved through `get_typed_annotation` goes through this function, so this breaks forward-ref resolution on older Pydantic and leaves the intended deprecation fix unused on newer Pydantic. The intended check is `if try_eval_type is not None:`. The test changes do not exercise `evaluate_forwardref` or string annotations, so the existing suite cannot catch this.

comments.body: The parity correction is inverted. The old code made `ub` odd by subtracting 1 only when it was even (`if not ub & 1`). The new code subtracts 1 only when `odd` is already odd (`if odd & 1`). After this, `odd` is always even, so `count(odd, step=-2)` only visits even numbers. Since every even number above 2 is composite, `first_true(..., pred=is_prime)` always returns 2 for any n > 1_000_000 with approximate=True. Every such call returns a wrong answer. The existing suite does not cover this branch, so it stays green.
